description: Native Land is a web map of Indigenous territories, treaties and languages around the world, drawn to represent nations and peoples on their own terms, with reference pages documenting the research behind each shape. The organisation reports more than 4,000 nations added, over 100 million visitors and more than 20 million API calls. It is made by Native Land Digital, a Canadian non-profit organisation. Coverage is global. The maps can be viewed online and the GeoJSON files and an API are provided free of charge; no licence is stated on the home page. Caveats: the organisation states that its maps are not official sources, boundaries overlap and are contested, and it corrects errors with input from the parties involved. For simulation it helps identify where mines, pipelines, dams and power lines cross Indigenous lands, which matters for consent, conflict and social risk in scenarios for critical mineral supply and infrastructure planning. It is related to the WRI global mining in socially vulnerable areas record in this catalogue, which also links mining to affected communities.
